questions.q: Why does assertEquals fail for AI answers?
options: The same correct answer comes with different words each time
questions.why: Test the meaning, not the exact wording.

questions.q: Which evaluator checks if an answer is supported by the documents (hallucination detection)?
questions.why: It asks the judge whether the claim is supported by the document.

questions.q: What does an EvaluationRequest contain?
options: The question, the retrieved documents and the answer

questions.q: In the lab, the judge replied 'Yes' plus an explanation, and the test failed. Why?
options: The judge model was too small
The evaluator only passes on a bare 'yes': a one-word prompt fixed it
questions.why: Read what your judge really says.

questions.q: How do you make sure your judge works?
options: Give it a wrong answer on purpose: it must fail
Use the same model as the app
questions.why: The lab's judgeCatchesAHallucination test uses '35 vacation days'.

questions.q: What do you add to see Spring AI's metrics?
options: Spring Boot Actuator (and a registry like Prometheus)
questions.why: Spring AI records Micrometer observations; Actuator exposes them.

questions.q: Which metric counts tokens, split into input, output and total?
questions.why: Tag gen_ai.token.type: input, output or total.

questions.q: In the lab, one RAG question used ~350 input tokens and 14 output tokens. Why so many input tokens?
options: The retrieved chunks are added to the prompt
questions.why: With RAG, topK and chunk size drive the cost.

questions.q: Where do you get the tokens of one specific call?
questions.why: Usage has the prompt (input) and completion (output) tokens.

questions.q: Why is spring.ai.chat.observations.log-prompt false by default?
options: Prompts contain user data: logging them risks privacy
questions.why: Turn it on only to debug, never with real user data.

questions.q: What is an indirect prompt injection?
options: Orders hidden in data the model reads, like a document in your vector store
questions.why: In the lab, a wiki page told the assistant to ask for passwords.

questions.q: In the lab, did a stricter system prompt stop the wiki attack?
options: No: the model still asked for the password
questions.why: A prompt is not a security boundary.

questions.q: Which two layers blocked the attack in the lab?
options: A bigger model and more chunks
Scanning chunks at ingestion, and checking answers in an output guard advisor
questions.why: Data and output checks, in code.

questions.q: Why does the OutputGuardAdvisor use Ordered.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE?
options: First in, last out: it sees the final answer after every other advisor

questions.q: A user used up their token budget. What does the API return?
questions.why: The budget is checked before each call.

questions.q: A good AI test strategy starts with...
options: Plain code assertions, then a judge for meaning

questions.q: The judge model should be...
options: The same model as the app, at temperature 1
A different (often bigger) model, at temperature 0

questions.q: The fact checker failed on the answer '14'. Why?
options: A bare number isn't a claim it can check: ask for full sentences

questions.q: Why keep evals out of every build?
options: They are slow (8 tests took ~3 minutes) and slightly unstable

questions.q: gen_ai.client.operation measures...
options: The time of each model call

questions.q: How do metrics reach Grafana?
options: Actuator exposes /actuator/prometheus, Prometheus scrapes it, Grafana reads Prometheus

questions.q: Estimated cost of a call =
options: Input tokens × input price + output tokens × output price

questions.q: Why not tag metrics with a user ID?
options: It creates one time series per user (high cardinality)

questions.q: Where can an indirect injection come from?
options: Documents, web pages or emails the model reads

questions.q: Which layer is NOT a security boundary on its own?
For tools that change data, the safest rule is...
options: Least privilege, and a human confirms irreversible actions

questions.q: Which three controls protect your bill?
options: maxTokens, an input length limit and a per-user token budget
More chunks, higher topK, bigger model

challenge.title: Make your own AI app production-ready
challenge.task: Take one app you built in this course (or your own) and add evals, metrics and guardrails.
requirements: A golden set of at least 8 questions, tested with plain assertions plus RelevancyEvaluator and FactCheckingEvaluator, and a judge on another model
One test that proves the judge fails a made-up answer
Actuator and Prometheus metrics, and an endpoint that reports tokens and an estimated cost
One real prompt injection attack you wrote yourself, blocked by a check in code (ingestion or output)
maxTokens, an input length limit and a per-user token budget
selfCheck: Your evals pass at least twice in a row
You can say how many input tokens one request costs, and why
Your attack works with the guardrails off, and is blocked with them on
